Example Data Entry Scenarios

In this section we will provide some examples of how data should be entered into the system for different clinical scenarios.

Example 1:

A patient presents with a new diagnosis of metastatic prostate cancer and receives radiotherapy to the bone and the prostate gland a month apart.

Steps for data entry:

  1. Enter patient data.

  2. Enter the diagnosis as Prostate cancer and choose presentation as Metastatic.

  3. Enter the pathology data for the sites from where the pathology was collected. For example if the patient had a biopsy of the bone lesion and the prostate gland then two entries for the pathology form will be required. In this situation, both pathologies will be related to the same diagnosis.

  4. Since the patient has received radiotherapy to the bone and prostate as two seperate courses, two form entries will be required for the two courses of radiotherapy. However they will be related to the same diagnosis.

Example 2:

The same patient presents after a year with progression of the disease and liver metastases for which radiotherapy was planned.

Steps for data entry:

  1. Add a new diagnosis as Bone metastasis for the same patient (do not create a new patient record) and choose presentation as Metastatic.

  2. If the lesion characteristics for the liver lesion need to be recorded, you can add a new entry in the Lesion form for the corresponding diagnosis.

  3. Enter the radiotherapy data for the course of radiotherapy to the liver noting the anatomical site as Liver.

Example 3:

A patient presents with the diagnosis of a metastatic lung cancer and has received radiotherapy to the brain.

Steps for data entry:

  1. Enter patient data.

  2. Enter the diagnosis as Lung Cancer and choose presentation as Metastatic.

  3. Enter the pathology data for the site where the pathology was collected e.g. the Lung lesion.

  4. Enter the radiotherapy data for the course of radiotherapy to the brain noting the anatomical site as Brain.

Example 4:

A patient presents with synchronous breast cancer and endometrial cancer and received radiotherapy for both the sites.

Steps for data entry:

  1. Enter the patient data.

  2. Enter the diagnosis seperately for Breast cancer and endometrial cancer. Note that DICOM series can be independantly linked to each diagnoses.

  3. Enter the radiotherapy data for the course of radiotherapy to the corresponding diagnoses.
